paper.title: HumanoidBench: Simulated Humanoid Benchmark for Whole-Body Locomotion and Manipulation
paper.source_version: arXiv v2, 2024-06-18; latest public arXiv version verified 2026-08-30. Published in Robotics: Science and Systems XX, DOI 10.15607/RSS.2024.XX.061. Official code evidence pinned to release v0.2.0, commit b917f7aa0890682e98ba5aa3f635fcd781d84936, 2024-07-01.

decision_relevance.why_admitted: HumanoidBench provides a public executable whole-body task surface, exact state/action/reward/termination contracts, flat-policy baselines, and source-located failure traces. It also shows that changing the action/controller through hand blocking or a pretrained reaching hierarchy materially changes learning, which defines a fixed-trainer boundary for Sam's two-knob harness.
not_evidence_for: reference-dataset selection, sequencing, composition, oracle guards, transitions, or recovery
automatic generation, repair, search, or ranking of executable task rewards
an independent objective evaluator for a changed task reward, because reported episode return reuses the training reward and success bars are qualitative
a reference-only intervention under a fixed observation, action, controller, reward, and budget contract
a fixed-trainer causal comparison between flat and hierarchical policies, because the hierarchy changes the high-level action interface and adds separate controller pretraining
multimodal policy performance despite implemented camera and tactile observations
hardware deployment, sim-to-real success, or real-world task validity

mechanisms.name: Executable whole-body benchmark runtime
mechanisms.description: HumanoidBench packages MuJoCo robot/task environments around a primary Unitree H1 body with two Shadow Hands. The paper defines 27 task families with task-specific reset state, observation additions, dense or sparse reward, termination, and horizon.

mechanisms.name: State-based 61-dimensional joint-target contract
mechanisms.description: The reported benchmark policies receive privileged proprioceptive and task-object state and issue 61 normalized joint-position targets at 50 Hz. The robot-only state is 151-dimensional; object state is task-dependent and additional.

mechanisms.name: Hand-authored dense and sparse task-reward suite
mechanisms.description: Task rewards compose shared tolerance-based posture and control-effort terms with task-specific distances, velocities, contacts, stage logic, and sparse completion bonuses. The formulas are environment definitions, not outputs of a reward-search method.

mechanisms.name: Training-reward return with qualitative success target
mechanisms.description: The learning curves sum the environment reward across each episode, average curves over three seeds, shade one standard deviation, and compare return to task-specific dashed lines that the paper calls qualitative measures of success.

mechanisms.name: Flat-policy algorithm benchmark
mechanisms.description: DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, SAC, and a four-task PPO subset are trained directly against the benchmark state/action/reward interface. Approximately equal wall time yields 10 million environment steps for DreamerV3 and SAC but 2 million for TD-MPC2.

mechanisms.name: Hand-action dimensionality ablation
mechanisms.description: The paper compares the full 61-dimensional action with a 19-dimensional action that fixes all 42 hand actuators to zero while retaining the 151-dimensional observation and hand mass. The reduced action learns faster on walk and shows a similar trend on push.

mechanisms.name: Frozen reaching-policy hierarchy
mechanisms.description: For push and package, a DreamerV3 or TD-MPC2 high-level policy emits one-hand or two-hand Cartesian reaching targets to a frozen PPO low-level policy. The low-level policies are separately pretrained in simplified MuJoCo MJX environments with force perturbations.

mechanisms.name: Pinned official benchmark release
mechanisms.description: Official release v0.2.0 at commit b917f7aa0890682e98ba5aa3f635fcd781d84936 contains environment code, learner adapters, pretrained reaching weights, training logs, and pinned core simulator dependencies.

failure_modes.name: Highbar contact-holding local behavior
failure_modes.description: The H1 conservatively maintains bar contact to avoid termination but fails to execute the required whole-body rotation, despite a dense reward.

failure_modes.name: Door latch without whole-body pull
failure_modes.description: The policy turns the door hatch but does not learn the coordinated arm pull and backward body motion needed to open and traverse the door.

failure_modes.name: Hurdle collision instead of jumping
failure_modes.description: The policy learns the requested forward velocity but adopts stable collision poses at the hurdle and does not explore the higher-reward jump.

failure_modes.name: Unused hand actions impede learning
failure_modes.description: Adding 42 hand actions substantially lowers walk and push performance even where dexterous motion is unnecessary; fixing them to zero accelerates learning while observations and mass remain.

failure_modes.name: Reaching prior does not cover lifting
failure_modes.description: The hierarchical package policy gets closer to pickup but struggles to lift because the low-level reaching policy never experienced lifting during pretraining.

failure_modes.name: Training reward is also the headline evaluator
failure_modes.description: The reported episode return sums the same environment reward optimized during training, and the dashed success lines are qualitative. Therefore a changed task reward changes the headline metric itself unless an external evaluator is frozen; this final sentence is a harness implication, not an author claim.

failure_modes.name: Equal wall time produces unequal sample budgets
failure_modes.description: Approximately 48 hours corresponds to 10M environment steps for DreamerV3 and SAC but 2M for TD-MPC2, so the reported cross-algorithm comparison is not matched by environment interactions.

failure_modes.name: Three-seed descriptive statistics only
failure_modes.description: Curves and tables use three seeds and standard deviations. The paper does not identify the seed values, report confidence intervals, or perform hypothesis tests.

failure_modes.name: Vision and tactile support are not benchmarked
failure_modes.description: The environment implements two head cameras and whole-body tactile sensing, but the paper evaluates only privileged state observations and leaves multimodal evaluation to future work.

failure_modes.name: Modified hand morphology and simulation-only evidence
failure_modes.description: The authors remove the Shadow Hands' forearms and explicitly call the resulting morphology not currently realistic. The paper does not report hardware transfer or real-world benchmark performance.

failure_modes.name: Average-versus-maximum return wording ambiguity
failure_modes.description: Appendix C-C says it reports mean and standard deviation of maximum episode returns, then captions Table V as average returns and Table VI as maximum returns. The table captions identify the two metrics most precisely.

evaluation.name: Twenty-seven-task whole-body evaluation suite
evaluation.description: Twelve locomotion and fifteen manipulation task families span 500-1000 control-step horizons under a shared H1-plus-hands action interface and task-specific object observations, rewards, resets, and termination.

evaluation.name: Flat DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, SAC, and PPO benchmark
evaluation.description: The paper reports three-seed learning curves for DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, and SAC on the suite and runs PPO on walk, kitchen, door, and package. Most final average-return rows remain below the qualitative task targets.

evaluation.name: Selected final-budget average and maximum returns
evaluation.description: Table V reports final average return and Table VI maximum return. Walk is above target for DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 in Table V; push has negative averages for all three flat baselines while DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 each have a 1000 maximum; all kitchen rows are zero.

evaluation.name: Full, no-hand, and blocked-hand action comparison
evaluation.description: On walk and push, the paper compares full hands, robot without hands, and a full robot whose 42 hand actuators are fixed. The blocked-hand action learns faster, isolating action dimensionality while retaining observation and hand mass.

evaluation.name: Flat versus frozen-reaching hierarchy
evaluation.description: On push and package, the paper compares direct joint-action policies with high-level policies using separately pretrained one-hand or two-hand reaching controllers. Push improves strongly; package improves less and still fails to lift.

evaluation.name: Qualitative behavior-level failure inspection
evaluation.description: The paper names and illustrates highbar contact holding, door partial completion, and hurdle collision as distinct failure behaviors behind low reward.

evidence.locator: arXiv record, submission history
evidence.claim: The paper was submitted 2024-03-15 and last revised as v2 on 2024-06-18; v2 is the latest public arXiv version as verified 2026-08-30.

evidence.locator: Robotics: Science and Systems XX paper record
evidence.claim: The work was published at RSS 2024 with DOI 10.15607/RSS.2024.XX.061.

evidence.locator: Section III, Simulated Humanoid Robot Environment
evidence.claim: The primary benchmark uses MuJoCo, Unitree H1, and two modified Shadow Hands; supports state, two-camera vision, and 448-taxel tactile observations; benchmarks state input; and uses a 61-dimensional action at 50 Hz.

evidence.locator: Table II, Humanoid robot specifications with and without hands
evidence.claim: With two hands the robot-only observation is 151-dimensional, action is 61-dimensional, body DoF is 25, and two-hand DoF is 50; without hands observation/action are 51/19.

evidence.locator: Figures 4 and 5 captions
evidence.claim: Curves average three seeds with standard-deviation shading; episode return sums per-step reward; dashed lines qualitatively indicate success; kitchen is purely sparse with maximum four.

evidence.locator: Section IV and Sections IV-A-IV-B
evidence.claim: HumanoidBench contains 27 task families: 12 locomotion and 15 whole-body manipulation tasks, with objectives enumerated by the paper.

evidence.locator: Sections V-A and V-B, Baselines and Results
evidence.claim: The paper evaluates DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, SAC, and a four-task PPO subset for approximately 48 hours; different algorithms reach different step counts; most remain below qualitative success targets, especially on long-horizon manipulation.

evidence.locator: Section V-C, With Hands vs. Alternative Configurations
evidence.claim: Fixing 42 hand-action dimensions reduces action size from 61 to 19 while retaining 151-dimensional observation and hand mass, and learns faster on walk with a similar push trend.

evidence.locator: Section V-D, Flat vs. Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
evidence.claim: Push and package use frozen one-hand/two-hand reaching policies beneath a high-level policy; low-level pretraining uses simplified feet-only collision models, no hands, link perturbations, 32,768 environments, 2B/4B steps and 36/60 hours; push improves strongly while package still struggles to lift.

evidence.locator: Section V-E, Common Failures
evidence.claim: The paper reports highbar contact holding without rotation, door latch actuation without coordinated pulling, and hurdle collision without jumping.

evidence.locator: Section VI, Conclusion and Future Work
evidence.claim: The experiments cover state-based environments only; multimodal evaluation, more realistic assets, and sim-to-real study are future work.

evidence.locator: Appendix B-A-B-C, Observation Space, Action Space, Simulation Performance
evidence.claim: The appendix specifies 151 robot-state dimensions, normalized 61-dimensional position actions, 0.002-second simulation timestep, 1050 FPS default throughput, and task-dependent environment-state additions.

evidence.locator: Appendix B-E, Task Specification shared definitions
evidence.claim: Shared reward primitives define the tolerance function, default head-height and upright parameters, small-control term, and stable standing product used across task rewards.

evidence.locator: Appendix B-E13, push
evidence.claim: Push uses a 1000 success bonus at box-goal distance below 0.05, unit goal-distance penalty, 0.1 hand-distance penalty, 500-step horizon, and termination on success.

evidence.locator: Appendix B-E23-B-E24, kitchen and package
evidence.claim: Kitchen rewards completed subtasks over 500 steps; package combines exact distance, posture, height, and 1000 success terms, terminates below 0.1 goal distance, and has a 1000-step horizon.

evidence.locator: Appendix C-A, Baseline Implementation Details
evidence.claim: Flat baselines use JaxRL Minimal SAC, Stable-Baselines3 PPO with four environments, DreamerV3 medium with UTD 64, and TD-MPC2 5M, otherwise named-code defaults.

evidence.locator: Appendix C-B, Reaching Policy Implementation Details
evidence.claim: Low-level reaching uses PureJaxRL PPO defaults except the environment count, 16 steps per environment, and entropy coefficient 0.001.

evidence.locator: Appendix C-C, Table V, Average returns
evidence.claim: Table V reports exact average return at 10M DreamerV3/SAC or 2M TD-MPC2 steps with standard deviation and task target across 31 named task variants.

evidence.locator: Appendix C-C, Table VI, Maximum returns
evidence.claim: Table VI reports maximum returns; the push row is 1000.0 +/- 0.0 for DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 and 352.8 +/- 31.5 for SAC against target 700.
